chunks: And it is narrated from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “I have abandoned trade.” So he said, “Do not do that. Open your door, spread your mat, and seek sustenance from Allah, your Lord.”

key_terms.بِسَاطَكَ: your mat or spread, referring to setting up one's place of trade
key_terms.رَبَّكَ: your Lord, the true source of provision
key_terms.لَا تَفْعَلْ: a direct prohibition against doing that act
key_terms.ٱفْتَحْ: open; an instruction to begin engaging in livelihood
key_terms.ٱلتِّجَارَةَ: trade or commerce as a lawful means of earning

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about leaving trade and seeking livelihood?
ai.summary: This hadith discourages abandoning lawful trade and earning a livelihood. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام instructs the questioner to remain active in seeking provision while relying on Allah as the true giver of sustenance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Al-Fudhayl ibn Yasaar asked Abu Abdullah (as): "I have abandoned trade."
Imam (as) replied: "Do not do that. Open your door, spread your mat, and seek sustenance from your Lord (azj), Allah (swt)."
